To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) angiotensin AT1 and AT1 receptor subtypes are involved in the development and maintenance of hypertension-induced vascular changes, (2) AT2 receptors are involved in the regulation of vascular tone, (3) AT2 receptor stimulation may prevent the development of hypertension, and (4) the relative role of the different angiotensin receptor subtypes in the development of hypertension is species dependent.

(i) angiotensin receptors are expressed by all the cells of the vasculatures; (ii) angiotension II receptors are involved in the response of vessels to arterial hypertension; and finally, that (iii) the relative role of AT1 versus AT2 receptors is different in different cells and different species, and depends on the experimental condition.
the renin- angiotensin system has an important role in the regulation of blood pressure, and the renin-angiostensin system has a role in the regulation the vascular structure and function.

the role of the angiotensin system in the cardiovascular system and in particular with the differential role of the AT1 and AT _{2} receptors in vascular cells.
the identification of the molecular mechanism of action of the renin angiotensin system in the vasculary.
the role of angiotension II in vascular structure and function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the AT2 receptors are involved in the regulation of the structure of the vasculatures in hypertension.
the AT2 receptors play a role in the regulation of vascular tone in some experimental situations and in some cell types.

the renin- angiotensin system plays a major role in vascular remodelling in arterial hypertension, but that this role is not limited to AT1 receptors, and that the AT2 receptor may play an important and still not well defined role in the vasculopathy of arterial hypertension.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the renin- angiotensin system has a pivotal role in the regulation of the structure and function of the vasculatures.

the AT1 receptor plays a major role in the pathogenesis of arterial hypertension, whereas the AT2 receptor is a potential therapeutic target for the prevention and/or the regression of the structural alterations induced by hypertension.
the AT2 receptor is not a ‘silent’ receptor in the vasculatures of normotensive and hypertensive animals.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the renin-­angiotensin-­aldosterone system plays an important role in the regulation of the vasculatory function and that this regulation involves several components of the renin­­angiotensinsystem, including AT1 and AT 2 receptors.
the renin- angiotensin system has a major influence on the structure of blood vessels, and that the AT2 receptor may be an important player in the regulation of blood pressure.
the AT1 and AT1 receptors have different effects in the vasculatory system, and this may have important implications for therapy.
